about.title: Moreno Valley Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Moreno Valley sits where the SR-60 meets the daily pull of commuters heading toward Riverside, and the collision record reflects that traffic. In 2025, the city logged 842 injury collisions, with 1,239 people hurt and 9 lives lost. Perris Boulevard, SR-60, Heacock Street, and Alessandro Boulevard carry the highest counts, and reports cluster on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., when the week's last drive home is underway. If you were one of those numbers, the aftermath probably feels scattered: a totaled car, a sore neck that got worse overnight, an adjuster who already left a voicemail. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Moreno Valley residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims in Riverside County and works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives most drivers two years to file, but claims involving a city or county vehicle can require notice in as little as six months. Reaching out early keeps your choices open.

whyChoose.title: Why Moreno Valley Drivers Use LawProactive

items.title: Evidence Fades Fast on Busy Corridors
items.desc: Skid marks on Heacock Street get driven over and nearby camera footage is often overwritten within days. An attorney can send preservation requests and gather records before they disappear.

items.title: You Can Decline the Recorded Statement
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may call quickly and ask you to talk on tape. You are not required to do so, and an attorney can handle those conversations for you.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you shared some blame, you can still pursue compensation reduced by your share. There is also no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a standard car accident case.

items.question: I was rear-ended on the 60 near Moreno Valley during Friday rush hour. What should I do now?
items.answer: Get any medical evaluation you have been putting off, because soft-tissue symptoms often show up a day or two later. Save photos, the CHP or police report number, and any dashcam clips before they are lost. Then reach out to us so an independent attorney can review your situation without charging you anything up front.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in California?
items.answer: Most injury claims must be filed within two years of the crash. If a government vehicle or public agency is involved, a formal claim may need to be filed in as little as six months. Because that window is short, it helps to talk with an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does it cost anything to use LawProactive or to hire the attorney?
items.answer: Our connection service is free, and we are not a law firm. The attorneys in our network work on a contingency basis, which means you pay no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case. You will discuss the specific terms directly with the attorney before agreeing to anything.
